- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.5) in recent days, model tends to underpredict; increase forecast slightly to align with bullish momentum.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.5), model often overpredicts; reduce forecast to reflect bearish pressure.  
- Model consistently overestimates early in the 30-day horizon (especially days 1–5), especially after sharp price spikes; apply downward bias to first 5 days.  
- After a price spike (e.g., >+3% from prior day), model often overshoots in the next 3–5 days; cap forecast at +2% above prior peak.  
- Model shows persistent mean reversion bias: if price is above 70, forecast tends to drop; if below 65, tends to rise — adjust for 1–2 day lagged mean.  
- Sentiment volatility (large swings) correlates with forecast error; when sentiment shifts sharply, reduce forecast confidence and apply smoother transition.  
- Forecast error is more pronounced in the last 5 days of 30d horizon — model often misses tail risk; add 1–2% buffer for volatility spikes in final 5 days.
